leads.summary: Crash watcher can replace an unrelated notification after the shell restarts
leads.consequence: A surviving crash-watch process remembers an id from the dead notification server. After a shell restart Quickshell allocates ids again from 1. If an unrelated notification acquired that number before the next crash, the watcher's -r replaces its contents and click action without a new onNotification, while the previously restored crash toast remains on screen. If nobody has that id, the replacement becomes a new toast and the previous restored one also remains, so deduplication fails across the restart. The test's fake server never resets ids within a watcher run and cannot detect either case. Clear the cached ids when the server's D-Bus owner changes, or use a stable group key in the shell instead of a cross-generation numeric id; cover the restart/id-reuse case.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (finding A); corroboration noted, no other change

leads.summary: Open PR #13159 has an incompatible critical-toast policy and could pass its tests without actually changing the service
leads.consequence: #13159 explicitly gives brand-named critical notifications (Chrome/Slack) a finite lifetime even without a sender timeout, using app as a third argument to durationFor on both restore and live cards. #13161 keeps all unrequested critical notifications, regardless of app, until dismissal and delegates to a two-argument wrapper. Both change precisely these same lines. If this service wins a merge while #13159's keepsCriticalOnScreen helper and its helper-only tests are accepted, those tests still pass but Chrome/Slack critical popups never auto-hide, defeating #13159. The maintainers need to choose/reconcile the policies and add a service-path assertion, rather than combine the hunks mechanically.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified via gh (coord/hunter/pr-13159.json/.diff: keepsCriticalOnScreen, durationFor app arg); Opus self-check re-confirmed; published as Related open PRs note without claiming test outcomes

leads.summary: Open PR #11782 also changes crash-loop deduplication, with mutually failing tests if integrated independently
leads.location: bin/omarchy-crash-watch:19-66; test/shell.d/crash-capture-test.sh:282-314; open PR #11782 crash-watch-test.sh diff lines 577-627
leads.consequence: #11782 replaces the 60-second dedupe plus -r with per-crash --group crash:<name> and --expire-critical -t 60000; it adds a watcher test requiring two sends for two adjacent crashes. Keeping #13161's watcher makes #11782's new test fail (the second crash is suppressed by default dedupe); keeping #11782's watcher makes #13161's new crash-capture-test.sh fail (it requires the second send to contain -r). Both branches also disagree on whether a critical sender-requested timeout needs a separate flag, and on the 30 s versus 60 s ceiling. Reconcile the watcher, contract and tests together if both are considered for merge.
leads.triage: factual parts verified via gh (coord/hunter/pr-11782.diff: --group, 60000 ms, dedupe removed); mutual test-failure claims not verified and not published

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13161#issuecomment-5823424846) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13161#issuecomment-5847358464), checked at `0eb4399c`.

**Verified:** The redesign resolves the earlier findings. Critical toasts wait again unless the sender asks for a timeout, and the new `durationFor` tests fail if either the flat cap or the old always-wait rule comes back.

| Earlier finding | Status at `0eb4399c` |
|---|---|
| Critical toasts no longer wait for the user | **Resolved.** `durationFor` returns 0 for critical with no requested timeout. None of the six senders listed earlier passes `-t`, so they all wait again, and `manual/35-networking.md:39` is accurate again. |
| Third-party critical notifications closed as Expired | **Resolved.** An unrequested critical toast has no countdown, so `ref.expire()` is never reached and `notify-send -u critical -A ...` keeps waiting. |
| Late escalation inherits the old countdown | **Resolved.** `onUrgencyChanged` and `onExpireTimeoutChanged` now reset `remainingLifetime`, alongside the existing summary, body and image resets (confirmed from source; not observed in a live shell). |
| Multi-monitor timers (pre-existing note) | **No longer affects critical toasts without a timeout**, which have no timer on any screen. It still applies to low and normal toasts, as at base, and now also to critical toasts that request a timeout (such as `omarchy-battery-low`), which at base never had a timer. A separate issue seems reasonable, as the reply suggests. |

**Verified:** Within one shell process, the `-p`/`-r` handling in `omarchy-crash-watch` updates one toast for repeated crashes of one program, keeps separate toasts for separate programs, and gives the next crash a fresh id after a dismissal.

### Stored crash-toast ids can outlive the shell that issued them

`omarchy-crash-watch` is its own long-running user service and keeps `notify_ids` for its whole run. The notification server is the shell, and each shell process hands out ids from 1 again (`docs/notifications.md:37`). The shell restarts under a running watcher, for example during `omarchy update`, from `omarchy-font-set` or `omarchy-refresh-shell`, and when the shell itself crashes. Quickshell v0.3.1 honours a `replaces_id` for any notification it currently holds, whoever sent it.

```text
shell process A: nautilus crashes   -> toast gets id 3, watcher stores 3
shell restarts:  ids start at 1 again
shell process B: Taildrop arrival   -> toast gets id 3
nautilus crashes again              -> watcher sends -r 3
                                     -> the Taildrop toast becomes "Process crashed: nautilus"
```

This was reproduced in a model: the real `omarchy-crash-watch` and `omarchy-notification-send` against a stubbed `busctl` that implements Quickshell v0.3.1's `Notify` id rules. It was not run against a real Quickshell server. Base leaves the Taildrop toast alone in the same scenario.

**Impact:** When the old id collides with a toast the new shell still holds, that toast's text and click command are replaced in place and never reach history. Waiting critical toasts stay held indefinitely, so a collision is plausible, though not frequent. When there is no collision, the server adds a new crash toast, next to the earlier one if that was still on screen at the restart and was restored from disk. As a result, a crash loop that spans restarts still stacks, and so does a crash loop of the shell itself, the crash the watcher's own comment calls the most worth reporting.

**Suggested change:** Forget the stored ids when the unique bus name that owns `org.freedesktop.Notifications` changes (for example via `GetNameOwner`), and add a crash-capture case in which the stubbed server restarts: it drops the ids it holds and numbers from 1 again. That approach has not been tested. It does not merge a new toast with one restored from disk. A shell-side per-program key matched against restored rows would cover both; open PR #11782 takes that route with `--group`.

**Correction to the reply:** The reply and commit `3bdce328` describe `omarchy-battery-low` as the one first-party critical sender with a timeout. `omarchy-capture-screenrecording` (lines 26, 79 and 234) and `omarchy-capture-screenrecording-with-webcam` (line 8) send critical with `-t 3000` or `-t 5000`. At base these waited; now they leave after the 8 s floor, including "Recording process had to be force-killed. Video may be corrupted." That may be what those senders intended, but the change is not mentioned. Suggested change: mention it in the description, or drop those senders' `-t` if their toasts should still wait.

**Optional test improvement:** In `crash-capture-test.sh`, each program crashes only twice, so the "different id each time" check compares one id with itself and cannot fail. The stub also numbers ids from 1, so a watcher that counts its own ids gets the same numbers the stub hands out. Two mutant watchers pass the shipped test: one that counts its own ids, and one that switches to a new stored id after each replacement. A copy of the test with the stub counter seeded at 40 and a third crash per program catches both mutants and still passes on head. Separately, the Service.qml call into `NotificationLogic.durationFor` is not pinned: swapping the `Low` and `Critical` arguments, so that low toasts without a requested timeout would wait forever, passes `notifications-test.sh`. A source regex like the file's other Service.qml checks would catch it.

**Related open PRs:** #13159 changes the same `durationFor` lines to give critical toasts from any app other than `notify-send` and `omarchy-action` a finite lifetime, even without a timeout. That is the opposite policy for those senders. #11782 changes the same crash-watch path differently: per-program `--group` toasts that expire after a minute, with the watcher's dedupe window removed. The two PRs overlap with this one and would need reconciling if more than one is taken.

**PR title:** The title still describes the flat cap; a title describing the current rule (critical waits unless the sender requests a timeout) would match the change.
